name: Home Insurance Purchase Journey
summary: Covers the journey from first price comparison through to policy purchase. Key drop-off occurs at the quote form stage where users abandon before seeing a price.

stages.name: Research & Compare
actions: Compares 3-4 providers on price comparison site
Checks excess amounts and coverage levels
thoughts: Do I actually need contents cover?

emotions.label: Anxious
emotions.description: Overwhelmed by options and unfamiliar terminology

painPoints: Too many options with no clear way to compare
Prices vary wildly and it is unclear why
opportunities: Simplify comparison view — highlight the 3 things that matter most
Show price breakdown explaining what drives the cost

stages.name: Enter Details (Quote Form)
thoughts: Why do they need all this information?
I do not have my property details to hand

emotions.label: Frustrated
emotions.description: Form feels long and demanding — many users abandon here

painPoints: Form requires information users do not have readily available (rebuild cost, year of roof replacement)
No progress indicator — users do not know how long the form will take
opportunities: Reduce required fields — pre-fill from public data where possible
Add progress bar with estimated time remaining

stages.name: Review Price & Coverage
actions: Adjusts excess to see price change
Goes back to comparison site to check alternatives
thoughts: What am I actually covered for?
Can I get it cheaper elsewhere?

emotions.label: Sceptical
emotions.description: Price has been revealed but trust is not yet established

painPoints: Unclear what is and is not covered without reading the full policy document
No benchmark — users do not know if the price is competitive
Adjusting excess recalculates the entire page, losing scroll position
opportunities: Coverage summary card — 5 bullet points of what is covered, 3 of what is not
Inline excess slider that updates price without page reload

stages.name: Purchase & Payment
thoughts: I hope I have chosen the right cover
Where do I find my policy documents?

emotions.label: Relieved
emotions.description: Task is complete but residual uncertainty about the decision

painPoints: Terms and conditions are long and legalistic
Policy start date is not prominent in the confirmation
Confirmation email does not clearly explain next steps
opportunities: Plain-English terms summary with the key commitments highlighted
Prominent policy start date on confirmation page and email
Clear next steps: download documents, set up online account, add to calendar

insights.text: 7 of 10 users could not explain what 'excess' means after reading the policy summary
Average form completion time is 8 minutes — 60% of users who start the form abandon before completing it
Users who adjusted their excess level were 40% more likely to complete the purchase — engagement with the pricing model builds confidence
3 of 6 interview participants said they went back to the comparison site after seeing the quote to check if it was competitive
